Building MelonUI

MelonUI targets .NET 10, with the binding generator targeting netstandard2.0. The repository has separate build entry points for the full solution and the portable core.

Building and Running Tests

MelonUI.Tests is an executable regression runner rather than a dotnet test adapter. --soak runs 500 MXML reloads to check cleanup. --gpu adds a Windows hardware test.

The full shader source build currently requires Windows because ComputeSharp's source generator invokes native Windows compiler APIs.

Building Local Packages

This script builds local 1.0.0 packages and checks them from separate application/plugin consumers. It does not publish to NuGet, create a Git tag or make a release.

The core runtime depends on Pastel and Wcwidth. Its package includes the binding analyzer. MelonUI.Shaders has the optional graphics dependencies.

Platform and Runtime Information

  • Runtime: Normal untrimmed/JIT .NET 10. Reflection-based MXML and arbitrary plugins are not supported as trimming/NativeAOT deployments in 1.0.
  • Platforms: Windows and Linux have been checked locally. Native macOS and more terminal/SSH environments still need hands-on testing.
  • File Browsing: Local directory enumeration is synchronous and is not a sandbox.
  • Text: Console widths are best-effort; some shaping depends on the terminal and font.
  • Graphics: Optional controls have device and main-thread requirements. Normal controls do not need a GPU.
  • Removed Prototypes: The image viewer, audio player, decoders and playback managers are not part of the core. Waveform takes peaks supplied by the host.

The library uses the MIT license. See LICENSE and THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md in the repository for licensing and dependency notices. The docs describe the current source and local packages, rather than claiming that a public package release has been made.

Building the Documentation

From docs/site in the repository:

There are no npm dependencies. The .NET example runner refreshes the API list and control output examples. The Node build creates static HTML in dist, which can be served by a static host, including from a subfolder.

The guide index is content/guides.mjs, with individual guides in content/guides/. Control examples are in content/controls.mjs. See content/STYLE.md for the writing and layout conventions used by these docs.
